questions.question:
D3 — Issue 1: Make Save the single primary action in the header?
Project/branch/task: main, /plan-design-review of the Settings Page plan, Pass 1 (Information Architecture).
ELI10: Right now Save, Reset, Cancel and Export all look identical. A user scanning the header cannot tell which button is the one they came for, so they hesitate or misclick Reset next to it. DESIGN.md already says Save is the only filled button (#1d4ed8 with white text, about 6.7:1 contrast) and the other three are neutral ghost buttons. This is Design Principle 2: every screen has a hierarchy.
Stakes if we pick wrong: ship as-is and every visit starts with a small puzzle; a misclick on Reset opens a discard dialog the user did not want.
Recommendation: 1A because it applies the existing DESIGN.md token with no new component work.
Completeness: 1A=10/10, 1B=6/10, 1C=0/10
Net: trading a few lines of button variant props for an unambiguous primary action.

options.label: 1A Filled Save, ghost others (recommended)
options.description:
✅ Save reads as the one primary action in the first 3-second scan of the header.
✅ Uses the existing Button primary and ghost variants from DESIGN.md; no new styles. (human: ~30min / CC: ~3min)
❌ Reset/Cancel/Export become visually quieter, so Export discoverability relies on its label alone.

options.label: 1B Filled Save, outlined Export, ghost Reset/Cancel
options.description:
✅ Save is primary while Export gets a secondary emphasis for users who come mainly to download.
✅ Still reuses existing Button variants if an outlined variant exists. (human: ~1h / CC: ~5min)
❌ Introduces a third emphasis level DESIGN.md does not define, weakening the single-primary rule.

options.label: 1C Keep four equal buttons
options.description:
✅ Zero implementation change to the header.
✅ Avoids any visual shift for existing users.
❌ Violates DESIGN.md and leaves users guessing which action is primary; Pass 1 stays at 6/10.
